payload.gap_claim:
SCAN FIRST, then the claim - the gap is only honest afterwards ([[meth-state-of-the-art]]). Note that running this scan properly is also its own first test: this retro found that v2 instructs the scan in guidance and collects it nowhere.

THE FIELD, as it actually stands. Code search for agents has converged on THREE LAYERS rather than one tool: exact matching (grep/ripgrep), structural matching (ast-grep, patterns over an AST), and semantic retrieval (hybrid BM25 plus dense vectors). The current consensus is sequential escalation - start exact, escalate to structural when the pattern is structural, reach for semantic only when the query is conceptual. On the read side, the pattern across agent harnesses is equally settled: offset/limit paging, a byte cap that REFUSES an oversized read and points the caller at search instead of silently truncating, and search returning path:line:text capped at max_results - all of it driven by context management rather than by ergonomics.

WHAT EACH ALTERNATIVE SHEDS, which is the claim:

- HAND-ROLLED SEARCH (what we have) sheds correctness and context: no context window, no globs, no multiline, no encoding handling, and - measured today - it answers confidently when its required args are missing. It also sheds maintenance we never wanted; there is no case for re-engineering ripgrep.
- SEMANTIC INDEXING sheds FRESHNESS, and that is disqualifying here rather than merely costly. Semantic indexes tolerate staleness by design; text search demands extreme freshness precisely when an agent reads back content it just wrote - which is most of what our agent does. An index would be stale exactly when it matters most.
- ast-grep SHEDS NOTHING WE NEED YET, and is consciously REJECTED rather than overlooked: our product is one TypeScript codebase where structural queries are rare, and the escalation model says adopt it when exact search stops answering, not before. Recorded as a rejection with its trigger, not as an omission.
- THE NATIVE AGENT TOOLS (Read/Grep/Glob) shed the RECORD and the ATTRIBUTION. They see the working tree only - and since i5d withheld iteration evidence from trunk, that means they cannot see any shipped iteration's evidence at all. They also leave no trace an owner can audit, which matters now that se.law-responsibility-never-delegates makes the owner accountable for runs they did not watch.
- v1 sheds nothing on tooling and is the wrong comparable here: v1's lesson is about the PROCESS half of this iteration (guidance and lints), not the tool half.

SO THE GAP, AS A CLAIM: every alternative gives you either freshness or structure or history or auditability, and none gives all four. Ours is the only position that can, because we are not building a search engine - we are composing ripgrep for the tree, git for the record, and BM25 for the ledger behind one lane that logs what was consulted. And the SECOND half of the gap has no comparable at all: no agent tool surface we scanned makes the machine compute the checks the agent would otherwise assert about its own work. That half is not a better grep; it is the reason the first half matters.
payload.why_now:
FOUR THINGS MATURED, and none of them is 'we finally got around to it'.

1. THE DEMAND SIGNAL FINALLY EXCEEDED THE COST OF IGNORING IT. Six se_help misses across three days on one capability, while every other missed capability was built within days. Today it stopped being an inconvenience and produced three hand-rolled workarounds and three design-doc-to-build losses in a single iteration.

2. THE DEPENDENCY OBJECTION DISSOLVED. @vscode/ripgrep ships per-platform binaries inside the npm tarball with no postinstall and no network access - so the zero-dependency stance was protecting distribution simplicity that ripgrep does not threaten. The owner reversed it explicitly: 'we overvalued zero dependency'.

3. THE RECORD MOVED OUT OF THE WORKING TREE. i5d's close-and-merge split landed this morning, and from that moment a working-tree-only search cannot answer 'what did a shipped iteration decide'. Before i5d this gap did not exist; after it, any search surface we build must span refs from the start.

4. DELEGATION BECAME THE DEFAULT AND EXPOSED WHAT IT RESTS ON. i8d self-blessed nine gates including every killer, and the defects that shipped were caught by the owner's thumb rather than by any check. se.law-responsibility-never-delegates then ruled that the answer is mechanical judgement rather than more human review - which turns 'lint what can be linted' from tidiness into the precondition for the autonomy the project is aiming at.

AND ONE THING THAT MATURED IN OUR UNDERSTANDING, not in the world: v1 is a BRANCH of this repository, not an external system. Three of the six misses asked for external-repo access that was never needed - git show and git grep against main reach v1 today. The critical path shrank while I was writing this.
payload.value_props:
TWO AUDIENCES, and they are not the same person even though one of them is a program.

PROP 1 - THE AGENT WALKING THE LOOP.
Audience: the agent, in any session, including one that has never seen this project.
Need: reach any source the process requires, and know every rule that binds the step in hand.
Outcome: the lane is the fastest way to work, so nothing is gained by leaving it.
Alternative: native tools plus hand-rolled scripts - fast, but blind to the record, silent in the log, and unbound by rules minted after the session's training.
Difference: reads that reach the tree, the record and v1 through one surface; guidance that arrives in the packet rather than waiting to be discovered.
Validation signal: hand-rolled workarounds per iteration.
NEEDS AND PASS LINES:
  need N1: read any source the process mandates | outcome: the design document and v1 are readable through the lane | PASS LINE: a 132k-char file is read in parts through se_file_read, and v1's checklist is read through the lane, both in ONE call each, in an iteration where no script is written to do it.
  need N2: find things without four attempts | outcome: one search answers with context | PASS LINE: locating a known line in an engine source takes ONE call and returns surrounding context - measured against today's four.
  need N3: know the rules that bind this step | outcome: applicable laws and methods arrive in the packet | PASS LINE: a packet at a state to which se.law-whitelist-guards applies CARRIES it, resolved, without the agent searching for it.
  need N4: edit many sites at once | outcome: a mechanical multi-site change is one call | PASS LINE: six call sites change in one atomic hash-guarded call, and the log shows one call rather than a script.
  need N5: search what shipped | outcome: past iterations' evidence is searchable | PASS LINE: a term that exists ONLY in a closed iteration's evidence is found through the lane, without checking out a branch.

PROP 2 - THE OWNER WHO OWNS AN ITERATION THEY DID NOT WATCH.
Audience: the owner, reviewing a run that happened while they were away.
Need: trust a self-blessed killer, and audit what it rested on.
Outcome: gates rest on computation where computation is possible, and the record distinguishes computed from asserted.
Alternative: read the agent's prose and hope; or stay in the loop and give up unattended runs.
Difference: lints judge the mechanical half, so the agent's word covers only what needs judgement.
Validation signal: defects caught by the owner's own use after a green gate.
NEEDS AND PASS LINES:
  need N6: mechanical checks are mechanical | outcome: checks that can be computed are not asserted | PASS LINE: at least the models-adhered, red-observed and requirement-field checks are decided by a lint, and their evidence carries the lint's verdict rather than the agent's sentence.
  need N7: a lint never parks an unattended run | outcome: every lint decides or defers | PASS LINE: no lint in the suite has a third outcome; a lint that cannot decide leaves the check as prose.
  need N8: the record survives carelessness | outcome: evidence outlives a deleted tag or a flagless push | PASS LINE: after deleting every iter/* tag locally, a closed iteration's evidence is still reachable from trunk by hash.
  need N9: the audit distinguishes computed from asserted | outcome: the owner can see which checks were judged by machine | PASS LINE: reading a grant's evidence, a computed check is distinguishable from an asserted one WITHOUT reading the prose.
payload.business_case: SKIPPED, with the reason recorded rather than left blank: there is no acquirer and no revenue to model - quackitect is the owner's own instrument, and this iteration buys capability for the owner and the agent, not for a market. The currency that IS worth stating is the one the record already measures: today cost three hand-rolled workarounds, three re-derivations of rulings the design document already contained, three release-gate rounds, and one wrong conclusion drawn from a confidently wrong search. If the next iteration costs none of those, the effort paid.
